Critics note his scheme actually undermines his own argument, since despite claiming to be black he was accepted only by a lower-ranked school while facing racial profiling. The author argues affirmative action remains necessary to address stark underrepresentation of minorities in medicine, noting Kaling herself benefited from a diversity program early in her career.

Argentina's Esperanza Base recorded 63.5°F (15.5°C) on March 24, possibly Antarctica's highest-ever temperature. The World Meteorological Organization is forming a committee of climatologists to verify the reading, with an official finding expected by late summer or fall.

U.S. officials say there is no set timeframe for an Iraqi-led offensive to retake Mosul from ISIS, walking back earlier suggestions of a spring assault. Officials cited progress against ISIS, including the recapture of Tikrit, but noted Mosul's larger population and strategic importance make it a far more complex target requiring patience and preparation.

Paddy Power apologized after deleting a tweet comparing Newcastle's losses at Liverpool's Kop to police killings of unarmed African-American men, calling it a joke that caused no intended offense. The betting company, known for publicity stunts, faced social media backlash demanding the tweet's author be fired. Liverpool won the match 2-0, moving to fifth place, while Newcastle suffered its fifth straight league defeat.

Philadelphia police added attempted murder to charges against Nyia Parler, 41, accused of abandoning her quadriplegic, cerebral palsy-afflicted son in a wooded park for over four days while she visited her boyfriend in Maryland. The 21-year-old victim, found dehydrated and malnourished, cannot be communicated with about how he ended up there. Parler, in custody in Maryland, must complete unspecified treatment before extradition to Philadelphia.

Kim Ki-Jong, the man accused of stabbing U.S. Ambassador Mark Lippert in Seoul on March 5, has been charged with attempted murder, assaulting a foreign envoy and business obstruction. Lippert suffered a deep facial gash requiring 80 stitches and cuts to his arm, but is expected to recover fully. Police say Kim, who has visited North Korea seven times and has a history of violent protest, attacked Lippert to oppose joint U.S.-South Korean military drills.

Jill (Duggar) Dillard, from TLC's "19 Kids and Counting," gave birth Monday to a 9-pound, 10-ounce son named Israel David, husband Derick announced. The baby arrived over a week past his due date; Dillard, a student midwife, said she remained calm despite the wait.

"Furious 7" is on track for a $135-138 million domestic opening weekend, the largest since fall 2013, bolstered by a record $60 million international take on Wednesday and Thursday. The film, the last to feature Paul Walker before his 2013 death, is playing in a franchise-record 4,003 domestic theaters and over 10,500 international screens. It stars Vin Diesel, Walker, Dwayne Johnson and Jason Statham.

Secret Service supervisor Xavier Morales has been placed on administrative leave after a female employee accused him of making sexual advances and physically assaulting her at an office party. Director Joe Clancy called the allegations "very disturbing," and the incident will be investigated by the Office of the Inspector General. It marks the latest in a string of scandals plaguing the agency over the past year.

Hillary Clinton is announcing her 2016 presidential candidacy with strong political experience but must avoid Al Gore's 2000 mistake of appearing inauthentic and relying on inevitability. She faces challenges including trust issues, energizing the Democratic base amid Elizabeth Warren speculation, gender bias, and managing Bill Clinton's unpredictable influence on the campaign.

Ferguson is undergoing significant leadership changes following the DOJ's report on racial discrimination in its police and court systems, including the resignations of the city manager and police chief and the election of two new black city council members. The DOJ will soon negotiate police department restructuring, potentially including a merger with St. Louis County police, but activists warn that lasting reform depends on sustained community pressure during these negotiations. The article argues Ferguson's governance flaws—weak elected officials versus powerful unelected administrators—mirror problems in suburbs nationwide.

Etihad Airways lost a passenger's cat, Felix, after his carrier was crushed during a flight from Abu Dhabi to New York's JFK Airport, and the animal remains missing nearly a week later. Owner Jennifer Stewart has enlisted a detection dog and wildlife traps to search for the cat, while Etihad says it is investigating and reviewing pet-handling procedures.

Louis Jordan, 37, was rescued after drifting for 66 days on his capsized sailboat off the Carolinas, having survived a storm that broke his mast and shoulder. He was spotted by the container ship Houston Express and found in surprisingly good condition, having collected rainwater and caught fish using his laundry. Jordan is expected to recover and return to his marina in South Carolina next week.
